Hannah Price’s deftly acted production...Take away the scenes at the start and very end...and you have some unique and resonant drama that makes The Girl Who Fell something oddly memorable.'
The Girl Who Fell resists the need for a perfect ending and is more powerful for it.
The first hour of this one-act play is stronger than the ending, which lurches into sensationalism and contains one too many plot twists.
The result is a believable and heartfelt account of a contemporary tragedy.
The Girl Who Fell deliberates the indeterminate nature of suicide in a fascinating way.

cn.t: Rutherford's exploration of teenage suicide and grief earns mixed reviews. Critics praise the nimble dialogue and strong performances, especially Claire Goose, but fault the play for cramming too many ideas into 100 minutes.
